lines: Ugh, that door's stuck again. Kick it, I'm not kidding.
Left, obviously. Right is where that thing came from last time.
No way we're going right, I still remember that smell.
Come on, you know the left route is shorter than that.
Hey, you want the ladder or the vent? I vote vent, I'm tired.
I'm not crawling through that vent again, my knees are done.
Fine, we go your way, but if we die I'm blaming you.
That door's been sticking all night. Put your shoulder into it.
Push, then pull, then push again. Yeah, it does that every time.
Ha, the door's jammed, so the wall is our new doorway now.
Third stuck door today. I'm starting to take it personally.
Who painted this door red? Doesn't matter, it still won't budge.
My shoulder's wrecked from that door. Someone else takes the next one.
Honestly, I'd climb the whole ladder before I fight that hinge.
Stop arguing and look at the map. Left corridor, I'm sure of it.
Okay, I'm holding the light, so I get to pick the route.
You always say left, and you're wrong about half the time.
Half the time you're right. The other half, I'm the one limping.
Stairs are out, great. The ramp's longer, but at least it won't collapse.
Watch your step on the stairs, the third one gives way under you.
I stepped on that stair and it cracked. Don't be me, okay?
Stairs are fine, my legs aren't. Let's take it slow, please.
My feet hurt, so if we're going up, carry me a little.
Hold my hand on the ramp, it's steep and I'm scared of it.
Ramp's steeper than I remember. Lean back and don't rush.
I hate that vent. It's cold, it's tight, and it smells like feet.
The vent's cold enough to hurt. Get in, get through, get out.
Keep your elbows tucked in or you'll scrape the whole way.
If you hear scratching in that duct, don't go looking for it.
Something's scratching in the vent again. Nope, we're going around.
I'd take the long way round with you over the short way alone.
Nobody crawls into that shaft without a rope. Nobody.
Fine by me, but I'm not hauling the heavy bag down that hole.
The ladder creaks like my old knees. Honestly, it's rude.
Careful, that rung snapped in half. Test every step, seriously.
Why is the ladder always the part that's falling apart?
I've climbed worse, but never with a bag this heavy.
Ugh, the cistern water's freezing. Just jump and get it over with.
I'm not jumping the gap. You jump, and I'll catch your bag.
Okay, but if I land wrong, I'm yelling at you the whole way.
Jump, roll, and try not to sit down in the puddle.
That fall rattled my teeth. Give me a minute before we move.
Hey, slow down, that floor is rotten. I can feel it sagging.
Don't stand on the cracked tile. Trust me, it's not worth it.
Left route's clear, but that hall still gives me the creeps.
The hall past the vending machines is quiet. Too quiet, honestly.
Stay near the wall and keep the light off unless you need it.
Bet the kitchen route is a dead end. It always is, right?
Dead end again. Who designed this place, a maze fan?
Turn back, that passage just loops us into the same mess.
We went in circles twice already. I'm not doing a third lap.
The guy up front says the atrium's open, so let's trust him.
Fine, I'll lead, but you're carrying the crowbar. Deal?
I'll cover you, but hurry up, I'm getting twitchy back here.
Somebody prop that fire door open before it slams on our heads!
Radio keeps crackling about the north route. I don't trust that thing.
I'd say the north route's flooded, but nobody listens to me.
My keycard's dead weight here, so the back door it is. Sigh.
The reader's dead, so my keycard is basically a fancy bookmark.
Lockpick clicked, so the bolt should slide right open now.
Nice work on that lock. I owe you a snack for it.
Did you hear that thud? Something's leaning on the door, maybe.
I heard creaking across the hall. Let's not open that one.
That door's opening on its own again. Nope, nope, nope.
The door's closing behind us, so get through before it seals!
Okay, I'm through, your turn. Don't dawdle, that door's mean.
The vent route drops us out over the atrium rail. Stay low.
Something's crawling in the ducts up there. Yeah, I'm sure.
Keep the grate shut, we don't want that thing following us.
Pull the barricade from the top, the bottom boards are rotten.
You two push the door, I'll cover the stairs. Let's go, let's go!
Pry that panel open with the crowbar, but watch those sparky wires!
Easy with the crowbar on those bolts. Slow and steady, no wild swings!
The lock popped! That heavy door swung open, finally, thank goodness!
Ladder's gone, so we're sliding down the shaft. Hold on tight, friend!
Jammed again! One more shove, come on, you've got this.
Stairs are clear. Head up, keep your head down, and don't be a hero.
Every time something shifts down there, that grate rattles and I flinch.
Bolt's rusted solid again, so the crowbar it is, sorry.
Thanks for waiting at the door for me. Really, thanks.
You always check the corners first, and I kind of love that.
